qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Insurmountable local route density, exclusive territorial bottling agreements with The Coca-Cola Company across 31 countries, and ubiquitous cold-drink placement provide substantial scale advantages; demonstrated strong pricing power (+8% price/mix in 2022-2023, +2-3% in 2024-2025) passing through inflationary input costs. Primary moat risk is that brand equity and concentrate pricing power belong to The Coca-Cola Company (KO), which can adjust concentrate prices over time.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Pillar 3 Balance Sheet, REJECT). Well-run territorial Coca-Cola bottler with unmatched route density and pack-price execution across Europe and Australasia, but unlike asset-light KO it bears heavy plant/fleet capex, a thin 10.7% 5-year median GAAP ROIC, and 4.99x LT debt/Net Income (€9.69B LT debt vs €1.94B Net Income) from debt-funded bottler acquisitions (Amatil, CCBPI), exceeding the 4.0x fortress balance sheet ceiling.
qualitative.evidence: CCEP is the world's largest independent Coca-Cola bottler by revenue (€20.9B in FY2025, operating across 31 countries). 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 10.68% (2022: 10.23%, 2023: 11.13%, 2024: 10.02%, 2025: 10.9% reported / 13.3% normalized), diluted by €17.0B in franchise intangibles and goodwill. FCF conversion is healthy at >100% of Net Income (€1.8B–€2.0B Owner FCF). However, balance sheet leverage is structurally elevated: LT debt of €9,692M vs cash of €918M and TTM Net Income of €1,942M yields LT Debt / Net Income of 4.99x (and Net Debt / EBITDA of 2.7x), failing Gate 6's <= 4.0x threshold.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
